$comment: Third-party agent skills vendored into .agents/skills: each copy is the SKILL.md an installed package ships, with the rewrites below applied, and is never edited by hand. `node tools/vendor-skills.mjs update` renders them from the installed packages and pins their versions and sha256; `pnpm agents:check` fails when a copy differs. Each rewrite must change the upstream text, so an upstream change fails the check instead of slipping through. Format: the header of tools/vendor-skills.mjs.

notVendored.playwright-cli/references: the playwright-cli skill points at them in the installed package instead (its `Specific tasks` rewrite)
notVendored.playwright-trace: not needed: skill e2e-test opens traces with `pnpm exec playwright show-trace`
notVendored.playwright-component-testing: this repo has no Playwright component tests (browser tests use Vitest)

drizzle-kit.licenseNote: drizzle-kit's package.json declares MIT, but the package ships no license file or copyright line, and its source repository (drizzle-team/drizzle-orm) is Apache-2.0 at the root. The copies are used under Apache-2.0, which also meets MIT's terms: .agents/vendor/drizzle-kit/LICENSE (written by hand: source, attribution, changes) and LICENSE-Apache-2.0 (the license text).

notVendored.drizzle-output-modes: reference: `pnpm exec intent load drizzle-kit#drizzle-output-modes` (allowed in package.json#intent.skills)
notVendored.drizzle-responses-and-errors: reference: `pnpm exec intent load drizzle-kit#drizzle-responses-and-errors` (allowed in package.json#intent.skills)
notVendored.drizzle-migrations: conflicts: it recommends `drizzle-kit push` for local iteration; this repo only generates and commits migrations (skill db-migration)
notVendored.drizzle-push: conflicts: this repo never pushes a schema; every change is a committed migration
notVendored.drizzle-pull: not needed: the schema is written in packages/db/src/schema, never introspected

rewrites.why: every `playwright-cli <args>` command runs as the pinned `pnpm exec playwright cli <args>` (Playwright 1.63 has the `cli` subcommand; no @playwright/cli package)
upstream installs a global `@playwright/cli@latest` or runs `npx`; here Playwright is pinned in the pnpm catalog
with: ## Installation
Playwright is a pinned dependency of this repo (the pnpm catalog). Run every command from the
repo root as `pnpm exec playwright cli <command>`: never `npx`, `npm install -g @playwright/cli`
or a global `playwright-cli`, which run another version.
- `pnpm exec playwright cli open --browser=chromium` opens the Chromium that
`pnpm exec playwright install chromium` installs (once per machine, and after each Playwright
bump); a bare `open` launches the installed Google Chrome.
- This checkout's URLs (the dev web server, the e2e one): `pnpm ports`. Skill `run-web` starts
the servers.
- Snapshots, console logs and other output land in `.playwright-cli/` (gitignored).
- Close the browser when you are done: `pnpm exec playwright cli close` (`close-all` for every
session). Its daemon keeps running until then.

rewrites.why: the references are not vendored: they ship with the installed version, and run tests with `npx playwright test` where this repo runs them through Nx
with: ## Specific tasks
Playwright ships more guides with this skill, for the installed version: request mocking, running
code, sessions, storage state, test generation, tracing, video and element attributes. They are in
`node_modules/.pnpm/playwright-core@<version>/node_modules/playwright-core/lib/tools/skills/playwright-cli/references/`
(`<version>`: what `pnpm exec playwright --version` prints), and spell commands `playwright-cli …`
and `npx playwright …`: run them as `pnpm exec playwright cli …` and `pnpm exec playwright …`.
Run and debug this repo's e2e specs through Nx, never `npx playwright test`: skill `e2e-test`.

rewrites.why: `drizzle-kit skills` installs `skills@latest` with a download-latest runner over the vendored copies
with: ## Staleness check
Skip it here. `pnpm agents:check` (part of `pnpm check`) fails when the installed drizzle-kit
ships other skills than these copies, and `node tools/vendor-skills.mjs update` refreshes them
from it. Never run `drizzle-kit skills`: it installs `skills@latest` through a download-latest
runner and writes unrewritten copies over these.

rewrites.why: no drizzle MCP server here; drizzle-kit runs in packages/db through `pnpm db:generate` and Nx, never npx
with: ## Surface selection
drizzle-kit exposes its verbs (`generate`, `push`, `pull`, `up`, `check`, `export`) over a CLI,
an SDK and an MCP server; all three return the same JSON envelope and take the same `hints`
array. Here only the CLI runs, in `packages/db` (its `drizzle.config.ts`): `generate` through
`pnpm db:generate`, `check` through the db project's Nx target. No drizzle MCP server is
configured.
- `pnpm db:generate <what>`: a new migration from the schema (skill `db-migration`). It takes one
name (letters, digits, `_` and `-`) and only `--custom`, `--output json|text`, `--explain` (a dry
run that writes nothing) and `--hints-file <file>` (a JSON file in the repo); it refuses
anything else. The envelope of a dry run: `pnpm db:generate <what> --output json --explain`.
- `pnpm nx run db:db-check`: drizzle-kit's consistency check of `packages/db/migrations`
(`pnpm nx run db:test` runs it first).
- `push`, `pull`, `up` and `export` are not used: every schema change is a generated, reviewed
and committed migration, which each deploy applies.
- Never `npx drizzle-kit`, a global `drizzle-kit` or a download-latest runner (`pnpm dlx`): they
run another version than the pinned one.
